documents.title: Guidance for Appropriate Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence Tools at Stevens
documents.summary: Short IT-division guidance for faculty and staff on using generative AI: align with security and privacy policy, get supervisor approval for new uses, use only licensed tools with Stevens data, and obtain extra review for grading, personnel and similar uses. It does not address student coursework or academic integrity.
documents.stance_why: The document does not ban AI, but it says 'Use of Stevens data is only permissible with licensed AI tools' and requires 'prior approval from your supervisor' for new AI uses, so AI is permitted only in narrow, approved ways; it sets no coursework rule. Both coders agreed on restrict.

units.why: The opening sentence tells users that AI use must align with 'Stevens' Information Security Policy, Privacy Policy, and any other relevant policies'; it binds everyone and is a compliance duty, so P77 and must.
units.anchor: ensure it aligns with Stevens' Information Security Policy
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on actor, phase, modality and type; they differed only on unit_stance (A restrict, B neutral). The sentence adds no limit on AI use itself, only a duty to follow existing policy, so neutral.

units.why: 'seek prior approval from your supervisor and/or department chair for new AI uses in your work' is an approval gate for new uses, so P65 fits partly and the modality is must.
units.anchor: seek prior approval from your supervisor and/or department chair for new AI uses
units.frag_end: new AI uses in your work
units.fit_note: The approval is of new uses of AI by a supervisor or chair, not a review of a tool or vendor.
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, B ta-staff. The document is addressed to employees (faculty and staff alike, 'your supervisor and/or department chair'), not only to staff, so all. Type, phase and modality agreed.

units.why: 'Always consider the risks and ethical implications' asks users to weigh ethics before using AI; advice, so should. P53 names ethical concerns but this sentence names no specific harm, a partial fit.
units.anchor: Always consider the risks and ethical implications
units.fit_note: Only asks users to consider risks and ethical implications; it does not name bias, harm or environmental costs.

units.why: 'additional consultation may be required' with the named offices (Sponsored Projects, General Counsel, HR, IT, Compliance) says who is consulted on some AI uses; P80 fits partly because no owner or enforcer is named.
units.policy: Depending on the AI use case, additional consultation may be required with the Office of Sponsored Projects, Office of the General Counsel, Division of Human Resources, Division of Information Technology, and/or the Office of Compliance.
units.fit_note: Names consulting offices for certain AI uses; does not name an owner who enforces or grants exceptions.
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, B ta-staff; the sentence addresses AI users generally, so all. A used topic privacy-data, B policy-evolution; the offices are consulted on data, compliance and IP questions, nothing about revision, so privacy-data. Type, phase and modality agreed.

units.why: The guidance lists 'data sensitivity, regulatory compliance, ethical implications, user consent, data privacy' as considerations; it points to data and IP protection (P50) but states no rule, so informs.
units.anchor: Key considerations include data sensitivity, regulatory compliance, ethical implications, user consent, data privacy
units.fit_note: Lists considerations (including IP and consent) rather than stating a protection rule.

units.why: The data classification standards are offered 'as a reference for potential use of AI' with 'general guidance' that is 'not exhaustive'; this frames how users decide which data may go to AI, a data-protection principle (P50), informs.
units.anchor: Data Classification Standards can be used as a reference for potential use of AI
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. Checked against the source: 'The Stevens Data Classification Standards can be used as a reference for potential use of AI. These examples provide general guidance and are not exhaustive.' is a real statement of how the classification table is to be used, so kept.

units.why: The table says 'Use of Stevens data is only permissible with licensed AI tools, including Microsoft Copilot for Web with Data Protection and Zoom AI Companion' while logged in; it restricts Stevens data to licensed named tools, so P92 (P50 is the general data rule but the specific demand is the licensed-tool requirement).
units.anchor: Use of Stevens data is only permissible with licensed AI tools
units.policy: Use of Stevens data is only permissible with licensed AI tools, including Microsoft Copilot for Web with Data Protection and Zoom AI Companion, while logged in via a Stevens account.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on actor, type and modality; phase differed (A during-work, B general). The rule is an institution-wide standing condition not tied to a stage of coursework or assignments, so general.

units.why: Under the 'Prohibited for AI Use' heading the table lists restricted data such as 'Any personally identiﬁable info', financial records, NDA records, IP and passwords; this forbids putting it into AI and protects confidential data, so P50, must-not.
units.policy: Restricted data, including any personally identifiable information, financial records, records and information subject to NDAs, intellectual property or proprietary information, and passwords, is prohibited for AI use.
units.fit_note: The source is a table whose columns are garbled in the extracted text; mapping the listed examples to the 'Prohibited for AI Use' heading (the Restricted class) is inferred from layout.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on actor, modality and type; phase differed (A during-work, B general). It is a data rule with no stage of coursework, so general. A's wording named 'Sensitive and Restricted' categories; in the text only the Restricted examples (PII, NDA, passwords) clearly sit in the prohibited list, so I follow B's narrower, source-faithful policy.

units.why: The sentence says use cases such as 'grading or assessment of student work' require 'additional review and consideration prior to use in AI'; it conditions AI grading on review (P101), not a ban.
units.anchor: grading or assessment of student work
units.frag_start: Certain use cases, such as grading
units.policy: Grading or assessment of student work requires additional review and consideration prior to use in AI.
units.fit_note: Review is required jointly with other uses; no approval chain or further conditions are specified.
units.resolution_why: A coded actor instructor, B ta-staff. Grading of student work is done by faculty (and TAs); the text mentions no TAs, so instructor. Phase, modality and type agreed.

units.why: The same sentence lists 'recruitment, personnel, or disciplinary decision-making, legal analysis or advice, security tools using facial recognition' as uses needing additional review; a review condition on decisions about people, so P73 though it requires review rather than a human decision.
units.anchor: recruitment, personnel, or disciplinary decision-making, legal analysis or advice
units.frag_start: Certain use cases, such as grading
units.policy: Recruitment, personnel and disciplinary decision-making, legal analysis or advice, and security tools using facial recognition require additional review and consideration prior to use in AI.
units.fit_note: Requires additional review before AI use; does not state that a human must make the final decision.
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all and phase before-course; B ta-staff and general. Nothing in the sentence limits it to staff, so all; a review gate before use is institutional set-up like the other gates, so before-course. A's wording covers the full list of uses in the sentence, B's only part of it, so I follow A.

units.why: The sentence requires review for 'any non-public use of non-licensed AI tools with click-through agreements', a review gate on unvetted tools, so P65.
units.anchor: non-licensed AI tools with click-through agreements
units.policy: Any non-public use of non-licensed AI tools with click-through agreements requires additional review and consideration prior to use in AI.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on actor, modality and type; phase differed (A before-course, B general). It is a review gate before use, consistent with the other gates, so before-course.

units.why: The guidance sends questions on privacy, compliance or security in AI use to 'Security@Stevens.edu'; it names a contact, a partial fit for P80.
units.policy: For questions regarding privacy, compliance, or security in the context of AI tools and their use, contact Security@Stevens.edu.
units.fit_note: Gives a contact for questions; does not name an enforcement body or exception process.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on all codes; they differed only on whether the anchor alone states the rule. The anchor omits the topic of the questions, so a normalized policy is kept.

units.why: 'Stevens Generative AI Overview contains several additional resources regarding AI' points users to further guidance, so P102 (informs).
units.anchor: Stevens Generative AI Overview contains several additional resources regarding AI
units.fit_note: Points to resources; does not impose a duty to stay informed.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B. Checked against the source: the sentence is present and directs users to further AI resources, a real (if minor) pointer, so kept.

notes: Single IT-division document aimed at faculty and staff; no student coursework policy. The data-classification table is garbled in extraction. Dropped B-only units: P05 (data class definition 'Public ... openly accessible', not a policy about AI use) and P49 ('Lectures with student identifiers'): in the table layout this item sits in the Sensitive column, not clearly under 'Prohibited for AI Use', so it would overstate the source.
